edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Atque ego in hac parte juste indignor ad hanc tam apertam et manifestam Stephani stultitiam, quod qui sic de episcopatus sui loco gloriatur et se successionem Petri tenere contendit, super quem fundamenta Ecclesiae collocata sunt, multas alias petras inducat et ecclesiarum multarum nova aedificia constituat, dum esse illic baptisma sua auctoritate defendit. Nam qui baptizantur complent sine dubio Ecclesiae numerum. Qui autem baptisma eorum probat, de baptizatis et Ecclesiam illic esse confirmat. Nec intelligit obfuscari a se et quodam modo aboleri christianae petrae veritatem qui sic prodit et deserit unitatem. Judaeos tamen, quamvis ignorantia caecos et gravissimo facinore constrictos, zelum Dei Apostolus habere profitetur. Stephanus, qui per successionem cathedram Petri habere se praedicat, nullo adversus haereticos zelo excitatur, concedens illis non modicam sed maximam gratiae potestatem, ut dicat eos et asseveret per baptismi sacramentum sordes veteris hominis abluere, antiqua mortis peccata donare, regenaratione coelesti filios Dei facere, ad aeternam vitam divini lavacri sanctificatione reparare. Qui sic magna et coelestia Ecclesiae munera haereticis concedit et tribuit, quid aliud agit quam communicat eis quibus tantum gratiae defendit ac vindicat. Et frustra jam dubitat in caeteris quoque consentire eis et particeps esse, ut et simul cum eis conveniat, et orationes pariter cum iisdem misceat, et altare ac sacrificium commune constituat.
pass_a_gloss: And I justly am indignant in this part at this so open and manifest stupidity of Stephen, because he who thus boasts of the place of his episcopate and contends that he holds the succession of Peter, upon whom the foundations of the Church are laid, introduces many other rocks and establishes new buildings of many churches, while he defends baptism there by his authority. For those who are baptized doubtless complete the number of the Church. And he who approves their baptism confirms that the Church is also there among the baptized. And he does not understand that he obscures and in a certain way abolishes the truth of the Christian rock, who thus betrays and deserts unity. Moreover, the Apostle testifies that the Jews, although blinded by ignorance and bound by a very serious crime, have zeal for God. Stephen, who preaches that he holds the chair of Peter by succession, is not stirred up by any zeal against heretics, conceding to them not moderate but maximum power of grace, so that he says and asserts that they through the sacrament of baptism wash away the filth of the old man, give as a gift ancient deadly sins, make sons of God by heavenly regeneration, and restore to eternal life by the sanctification of the divine washing. He who thus concedes and grants great and heavenly gifts of the Church to heretics, what else does he do than communicate with those to whom he defends and vindicates so much grace? And he doubts in vain whether he also consents to the others and is a partaker, so that he also agrees with them and mixes prayers equally with them, and establishes a common altar and sacrifice.

pass_b_english: I am justly indignant at Stephen's stupidity, which is so open and manifest. He boasts of his episcopal see and claims to hold Peter's succession, upon whom the foundations of the Church are laid. Yet he introduces many other rocks and establishes new buildings for many churches, while defending baptism there by his own authority. Those who are baptized doubtless complete the Church's number. Whoever approves their baptism confirms that the Church exists among the baptized as well. He fails to understand that he obscures and, in a sense, abolishes the truth of the Christian rock by betraying and deserting unity. Meanwhile, the Apostle testifies that the Jews, though blinded by ignorance and bound by a most serious crime, have zeal for God. Stephen, who proclaims he holds Peter's chair by succession, is stirred by no zeal against heretics. He concedes to them not moderate but maximum power of grace, so that he says and asserts they wash away the filth of the old man through the sacrament of baptism, forgive ancient deadly sins, make them sons of God by heavenly regeneration, and restore them to eternal life by the sanctification of the divine washing. When he thus grants and attributes such great and heavenly gifts of the Church to heretics, what else does he do but communicate with those whose grace he defends and vindicates? And he doubts in vain whether he also consents to the rest and becomes a partaker with them, so that he agrees with them, mixes prayers equally with them, and establishes a common altar and sacrifice.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The translation of 'donare antiqua mortis peccata' as 'give as a gift ancient deadly sins' (Pass A) and 'forgive ancient deadly sins' (Pass B) both capture the sense of the Latin 'donare' (to give/bestow/grant) in this context, with Pass B being a more idiomatic rendering of the theological concept. All clauses, including the complex description of the sacraments and the reference to the Apostle's view of the Jews, are preserved.
